reference.source: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics / Gorlin's Syndromes of the Head and Neck
clinicalPearls: A severe autosomal recessive DNA-repair disorder within the nucleotide-excision-repair spectrum, overlapping clinically with Cockayne syndrome
Characterised by microcephaly with brain malformation, congenital cataracts and/or microphthalmia, a characteristic facial appearance and multiple joint contractures (arthrogryposis)
Prenatal or early-onset growth failure and profound developmental impairment are typical
Progressive neurological deterioration, feeding difficulty and recurrent respiratory infection are common
Caused by variants in nucleotide-excision-repair genes such as ERCC1, ERCC2, ERCC5 and ERCC6, linking it to Cockayne syndrome and xeroderma pigmentosum
Historically labelled Pena-Shokeir syndrome type 2, but distinct from the akinesia-based Pena-Shokeir type 1
Management is supportive and palliative, with genetic counselling for the recessive inheritance
reference.pathophysiology: Cerebro-oculo-facio-skeletal syndrome is caused by biallelic variants in genes of the nucleotide-excision-repair pathway (including ERCC1, ERCC2, ERCC5 and ERCC6), the same pathway disrupted in Cockayne syndrome and xeroderma pigmentosum. Defective repair of transcription-coupled DNA damage impairs the survival and function of neurons and other cells during development, producing microcephaly, brain malformation and progressive neurodegeneration. Associated foetal neurological impairment reduces movement in utero, leading to arthrogryposis, while abnormal development gives the ocular anomalies (cataract, microphthalmia) and the distinctive facial features. The disorder lies on a continuum with Cockayne syndrome, representing a severe, early-onset end of that spectrum.
additionalDifferentials: Pena-Shokeir syndrome type 1 (foetal akinesia deformation sequence)
Congenital cytomegalovirus and other congenital infections
Congenital muscular dystrophies with brain and eye involvement
Peroxisomal disorders such as Zellweger syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Neuroimaging showing microcephaly, calcification and structural brain malformation
Ophthalmological examination for cataract, microphthalmia and retinal changes
Molecular genetic testing for nucleotide-excision-repair genes (ERCC1/2/5/6 and related)
DNA-repair functional studies in cultured fibroblasts where genetics is inconclusive
Assessment of feeding, swallowing and respiratory function
Skeletal survey to characterise contractures and exclude other diagnoses
redFlags: Progressive neurological deterioration and intractable feeding difficulty
Failure to thrive with severe growth failure
Recurrence risk in future pregnancies given autosomal recessive inheritance
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is very poor, with most affected children dying in early childhood from neurological deterioration and respiratory complications; care is supportive and palliative, focused on comfort, feeding support and family counselling.
pitfalls: Confusing the DNA-repair-based COFS syndrome with the akinesia-based Pena-Shokeir type 1 despite the shared eponym
Overlooking the link to Cockayne syndrome and the wider nucleotide-excision-repair spectrum
Missing congenital cataract or microphthalmia on examination
Failing to provide recurrence counselling for the recessive inheritance
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
Gorlin's Syndromes of the Head and Neck
